title: Amines & amino acids
examples: What makes some amines more basic than others?
How is the structure of a peptide bond formed?
Can you explain what a zwitterion actually is?

explain.say: Today we are learning about amines and amino acids.
Amines are organic compounds containing nitrogen.
The basicity of an amine depends on the electron donating ability of its groups.
Amino acids have both an amino group and a carboxyl group.

draw.text: Amino acid structure: NH2 and COOH

explain.say: At physiological pH, amino acids often exist as zwitterions.
Peptides are chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds.

faq.q: What is the difference between an amine and an aliphatic amine?
faq.a: An amine is the general class of compounds containing nitrogen. An aliphatic amine is one where the nitrogen is attached to carbon atoms, not aromatic rings.
asks: What kind of nitrogen is in an amine?

faq.q: Why are zwitterions important in biology?
faq.a: Zwitterions allow amino acids to exist in a neutral, but charged, state in solution. This is crucial for protein structure and function.
asks: What is the charge state of an amino acid?
How do amino acids carry charges?

faq.q: How is the peptide bond formed between amino acids?
faq.a: The peptide bond forms through a dehydration reaction, where a molecule of water is removed from the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of the next.
asks: Do amino acids lose water to link up?

faq.q: Does the basicity of an amine depend on its structure?
faq.a: Yes, the basicity is influenced by resonance effects and the electron-donating nature of the attached alkyl groups. Electron donation increases basicity.
asks: Can I make an amine more basic?

faq.q: What is the general structure of a peptide?
faq.a: A peptide is simply a short chain of amino acids joined together. The linkage itself is the peptide bond.
asks: What is a small protein chain?

facts: Amines are bases because the nitrogen atom has a lone pair of electrons.
In a zwitterion, the amino group is protonated, and the carboxyl group is deprotonated.
Peptide bonds are formed by the condensation reaction between amino acids.
The basicity of an amine increases with increasing electron donation to the nitrogen atom.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes the basicity trend for amines?

options.show: Primary amines are always the most basic
options.say: Primary amines are always the most basic

options.show: The number of carbons always determines basicity
options.say: The number of carbons always determines basicity

quiz.why: Alkyl groups are electron-donating, which increases the electron density on the nitrogen, making it a stronger base.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because secondary and tertiary amines can be more basic depending on the groups.
wrong.2: This is tempting because resonance can pull electron density away from the nitrogen.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the type of carbon group matters more than just the count.

quiz.say: What is the charge state of an amino acid at physiological pH?

options.show: Depends only on the R group
options.say: Depends only on the R group

quiz.why: At physiological pH, the amino group accepts a proton and the carboxyl group donates a proton, resulting in a net neutral charge.

wrong.0: The basicity and acidity of the amino and carboxyl groups are also critical factors.
wrong.2: This ignores the deprotonation of the carboxyl group which is common.
wrong.3: This ignores the protonation of the amino group which is common.

quiz.say: What type of bond links amino acids into a peptide chain?
quiz.why: The peptide bond is a specific type of amide bond formed by the removal of water molecules.

wrong.0: The formation process always involves the removal of water molecules.
wrong.1: While charges are involved, the covalent linkage itself is the amide bond.
wrong.3: Ester bonds are formed from alcohols and carboxylic acids, not amino acids.
